གསུངས་པའོ། །རྟོགས་པ་ཡོངས་སུ་དག་པ་ནི་རྣམ་པ་བཞི་སྟེ། མངོན་སུམ་གྱི་#ཤེས་པས་ཤིན་ཏུ་རྣམ་པར་ངེས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རབ་ཏུ་རྟོགས་པ་ཡོངས་སུ་དག་པ་ནི་གང་གི་ཕྱིར། ཡིད་གཉིས་དང་ནེམ་ནུར་དང་བྲལ་བ་ཞེས་གསུངས་པའོ། །བསྒོམ་པའི་ལམ་ན་ཉེ་བའི་ཉོན་མོངས་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་

པ་ལ་རབ་ཏུ་གནས་པ། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་འདི་དག་ལ་གཞན་གྱི་དྲིང་མི་འཇོག་པ་ཤ་སྟག་འདུས་མོད་ཀྱི། འོན་ཀྱང་གཞན་དག་བསམ་གྱིས་མི་ཁྱབ་པའི་གནས་འདི་ལྟ་བུ་འདི་ཐོས་པར་གྱུར་ལ། ཐོས་ནས་ཀྱང་ཡིད་གཉིས་དང་ནེམ་ནུར་སྐྱེ་བར་གྱུར་ན། དེ་ནི་དེ་དག་ལ་ཡུན་རིང་པོར་ཕན་པ་མེད་
span: "perfectly accumulated the collections." Purity of application by being endowed with many qualities such as having few desires while seeking what is virtuous in the effort to comprehend is what is meant by "endowed with immeasurable qualities." Purity of realization is fourfold: purity of thorough realization because of being perfectly certain through direct knowledge is what is meant by "free from hesitation and doubt." Purity of the non-movement of afflictions, because no secondary afflictions arise on the path of meditation, is what is meant by "without afflictions." Purity of not being content, because one does not desire the Lesser Vehicle but desires to obtain the higher distinctions, is what is meant by "well-established in superior intention and conviction." In that regard, "superior intention" is faith and aspiration. "Conviction" is holding the objects of those as qualities. Purity of being independent of others regarding instructions and teachings, because one has correctly entered by oneself into the movement toward the final goal, is what is meant by "not dependent on others regarding these Buddha-dharma." Vajragarbha said: "O Son of the Conqueror, this assembly is indeed composed of perfectly pure Bodhisattvas who have perfectly purified their superior intention, perfectly purified their conceptual thinking, perfectly practiced what is to be practiced, made offerings to many billions of Buddhas, perfectly accumulated the collections, are endowed with immeasurable qualities, are free from hesitation and doubt, are without afflictions, are well-established in superior intention and conviction, and are a gathering consisting entirely of those who are not dependent on others regarding these Buddha-dharma. However, if others were to hear such an inconceivable state as this, and having heard it, hesitation and doubt were to arise, it would be of no benefit to them for a long time

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
Why is it "perfectly gathered"? Because the text says, "they have perfectly gathered the accumulations." Why is it "perfectly purified application" by possessing many qualities such as having few desires while seeking what is virtuous to be practiced for the sake of understanding? Because the text says, "possessing immeasurable virtues." 

Perfectly purified realization is of four types. Why is it "perfectly purified high realization" because of being perfectly and thoroughly certain through direct perception <note>literally: direct knowledge</note>? Because the text says, "free from doubt and hesitation." 

Since all secondary afflictions do not arise on the path of meditation, why is it "perfectly purified non-occurrence of afflictions"? Because the text says, "without afflictions." 

Since they do not desire the Lesser Vehicle <term>Hinayana</term> <gloss>the fundamental vehicle focused on individual liberation</gloss> but desire to obtain the distinctions of the higher one <note>the Mahayana</note>, why is it "perfectly purified non-attachment to mere sufficiency"? Because the text says, "firmly abiding in high resolve and devotion." In this context, "high resolve" refers to faith and aspiration. "Devotion" refers to apprehending their objects of focus as qualities. 

Because they have correctly entered into the movement toward the final goal by themselves, why is it "perfectly purified non-dependence on others regarding instructions"? Because the text says, "they do not depend on others regarding these Buddha-dharmas." 

Vajragarbha said: "O Son of the Conqueror! This assembly consists solely of perfectly pure Bodhisattvas. They have perfectly purified their high resolve, perfectly purified their conceptions, and perfectly practiced what is to be practiced. They have made offerings to many billions of Buddhas, perfectly gathered the accumulations, and possess immeasurable virtues. They are free from doubt and hesitation, without afflictions, and firmly abide in high resolve and devotion. They do not depend on others regarding these Buddha-dharmas. However, if others were to hear such an inconceivable state as this, and having heard it, doubt and hesitation were to arise, it would not be of benefit to them for a long time."
